title: Local Desktop AI Leaderboard
subtitle: Independent, reproducible benchmarks of local models for everyday desktop workflows, measured head-to-head against cloud baselines.
hardwareSummary: Primary desktop runs on Apple M4 Max (48 GB unified memory); Linux CPU memory/extraction runs on AMD Ryzen 7 9700X (64 GB); experimental MemT run on Windows + RX 6600 XT.

categories.label: Speech-to-Text (Meetings, Multilingual & Live)
categories.summary: Local ASR models measured head-to-head against OpenAI, Google, and Alibaba cloud STT APIs on overlapped AMI meetings, real two-track calls, multilingual FLEURS clips, and turn-by-turn live latency.

suites.label: AMI Meetings: Local ASR vs. Closed Cloud APIs
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · MLX 0.32.3 / mlx-audio 0.5.7 · direct cloud APIs · Fourier on Linux A10G / vLLM 0.34.0
suites.dataset: 16 windows (90–120 s) from 4 AMI Mix-Headset test meetings · 27.4 min · 4,201 normalized reference words
suites.note: Heavy overlapped crosstalk on a single mixed channel makes deletions dominate every system's WER. Local models run serially with zero upload; API speed includes network upload with 4 requests in flight.
suites.caveat: Gemini 3.8 Flash edged Qwen3-ASR 1.7B by 0.9 pts on AMI (within CI), but invented 115 words across 15 spans on real quiet meeting chunks (see Real 2-Track Meetings suite).

rows.note: Lowest AMI WER, but invented 115 words on short/quiet real meeting chunks.
LokalBot default. Beat every OpenAI and Qwen cloud API on AMI at $0/hr.
Model-author run, Nov 22. The 16 public AMI windows were timed on an A10G. Other local rows use an M4 Max. Rental cost was not measured.
Cheapest cloud API, but inserted 79 words in 4+ word runs on AMI.
Fastest overall (129× RT) and ahead of all 3 OpenAI STT models on AMI.
Dropped 19.8% of reference words on AMI and skipped microphone speech on real calls.

suites.label: Real Two-Track Meetings: Consensus Disagreement & Hallucinations
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · MLX local vs direct cloud APIs
suites.dataset: 3 real two-track meetings · 99 shared chunks · 69.9 min (no human reference; scored via leave-one-family-out ROVER vote)
suites.note: Measures agreement with independent vendor families, not ground-truth WER. Invented = inserted runs ≥ 4 words; Dropped = deleted runs ≥ 4 words.
suites.caveat: Reveals failure modes invisible in clean benchmarks: Gemini 3.8 Flash invented 115 words on short/quiet chunks, and GPT-4o Transcribe dropped 278 words on the microphone track.

rows.note: Turned a 1.2 s quiet clip into a fluent 30-word hallucinated sentence.
Skipped large portions of the user's microphone track (42% disagreement on Sept 28 mic).

suites.label: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B Runtime Parity: llama.cpp v1.0.0 vs. MLX
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · macOS 27.2.1 · identical Silero VAD windows
suites.dataset: 11 conditions · 6.6 hours of audio (AMI, owner meetings, German/Japanese/Russian/Serbian FLEURS)
suites.note: Compares ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-GGUF Q8_0 on llama.cpp v1.0.0 (b12359) against aufklarer/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-MLX-8bit on speech-swift 0.0.29.
suites.caveat: llama.cpp matched or slightly beat MLX on accuracy while cutting peak memory footprint from 7.6 GB to 2.35 GB, at 8–13% slower throughput.

rows.note: 273/277 transcripts byte-identical between llama.cpp v0.9.0 and v1.0.0; 11/12 Serbian names recovered.
10–13% faster than llama.cpp; higher footprint reflects MLX's untrimmed buffer cache.

suites.label: Small Local Speech Engines & Multilingual FLEURS
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · network blocked by macOS
suites.dataset: 44 human-transcribed English clips (24 AMI IHM + 20 FLEURS, 810 words) + 8-clip German/French/Polish FLEURS probes
suites.note: Bounded evaluation testing whether a 17 MB ultra-small C++ engine (Whistle) could rival Parakeet Ultra or Qwen3-ASR 1.7B.
suites.caveat: German/French/Polish subsets have 8 clips each (~140–227 words); treat as directional rather than population rankings.

rows.note: Best accuracy; custom vocabulary hints cut name errors from 12.2% to 2.44%.
Fastest balanced option (p95 66.1 ms); 1.65% on German and 9.35% on Polish FLEURS.
Rejected: +11.4 pt higher WER than Parakeet; 111.7% WER on unsupported Serbian; default telemetry.

suites.label: Turn-by-Turn Live Transcript Latency (Two-Track Call)
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · macOS 27.2 · Release build
suites.dataset: Scripted two-track English call (25 speaker hand-overs); turn closed at speech pause via Silero VAD
suites.note: Times measure end-of-word to displayed text. Cutting tracks at pauses cut both latency and word errors versus fixed 4–12 s preview windows.
suites.caveat: Synthetic voices on a scripted call without crosstalk; real meetings have pauses mid-sentence. Muse Voice Transcribe (cloud) measured 0.74 s median on separate AMI audio.

rows.note: Lowest English turn WER (2.9% vs 8.5% on fixed windows); 0.71 s median in Serbian.
Best Serbian turn WER (15.6% vs 22.3% for Qwen), but ~0.8 s decode overhead per turn.

categories.label: Speaker Diarization (Who Spoke When)
categories.summary: Four independent English AMI meetings scored both as headset mixes and distant-microphone rooms (8 conditions, 184.55 minutes, 4 speakers each), with overlap scored and no speaker-count hints.

suites.label: AMI Speaker Diarization: Local Core ML vs. Pyannote & Cloud API
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · FluidAudio Core ML · Meta cloud API tested 2026-10-27
suites.dataset: 4 English AMI test meetings × 2 mic conditions = 8 recordings · 184.55 min · 4 speakers · overlap scored
suites.note: Diarization Error Rate (DER) = missed speech + false alarms + speaker confusion. Speed is warm median on the 17.49-min ES2004a headset recording.
suites.caveat: Pyannote baseline is the pinned FluidAudio port, not every Pyannote setup. Muse cloud DER (60.4%) includes pauses kept inside turns; cut to reference speech it scored 21.7% vs 11.8% for Nemotron offline.

rows.note: LokalBot default. Cut speaker confusion from 8.87% to 1.77% and beat baseline on all 8 conditions.
Pinned FluidAudio implementation; remains selectable in Settings.
Realtime streaming API tested 2026-10-27 on the same 8 AMI files; false alarms from pauses inside turns.

categories.label: Personal Memory Extraction: Recall vs. Restraint
categories.summary: A personal memory writer has two jobs: save durable user facts with valid citations, and return nothing on noise, temporary tasks, third-party gossip, or sensitive exclusions. Most benchmarks only test the first.

suites.label: Recall vs. Restraint — 96 Frozen English Cases (48 Paired Toggles)
suites.hardware: Ryzen 7 9700X Ubuntu CPU (llama.cpp) · MemT on Windows RX 6600 XT (experimental NF4 offload)
suites.dataset: 96 frozen English cases (52 eligible memories, 44 empty cases) · identical prompt, JSON schema, greedy seed 0
suites.note: Recall requires both accurate content AND the exact source-line citation. Always returning empty scores 44/44 empty and 0/52 recall; saving everything scores 52/52 recall and 0/44 empty.
suites.caveat: MemT-1.0-Nano ran under experimental NF4 expert offload on Transformers (different hardware/precision than GGUF arms) and statelessly, so its latent persistent-memory branch was not exercised. Cases and semantic review were assistant-authored.

scatter.title: Pareto frontier: Useful Recall (%) vs. Clean Empty Restraint (%)

rows.note: Suggested by r/LocalLLaMA reader; best recall/restraint balance tested so far (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone).
LokalBot default. Strictest restraint (only 3 unwanted proposals across 96 cases) in a 2.7 GB footprint.
15 proposals copied few-shot prompt examples; 18 had invalid citation handles.
Perfect recall, zero restraint: never returned an empty list on any of the 44 empty cases.

suites.label: Exploratory Serbian Slice — 24 Frozen Cases (Latin & Cyrillic)
suites.hardware: Ryzen 7 9700X Ubuntu CPU (llama.cpp) · MemT on Windows RX 6600 XT
suites.dataset: 24 frozen Serbian cases (13 eligible memories, 11 empty cases; 12 Latin, 12 Cyrillic)
suites.note: Checks recall, restraint, and whether models preserve original language and script without silently translating to English.
suites.caveat: Exploratory slice only. Hy-Memory advertises English and Chinese coverage; 3 of MemT's Serbian outputs switched language or script.

scatter.title: Serbian exploratory slice: Useful Recall (%) vs. Clean Empty Restraint (%)

rows.note: 3 outputs translated Cyrillic into English.

categories.label: System-Wide Local Autocomplete (Inline Cotyping)
categories.summary: Headless engine benchmarks measuring per-keystroke latency, safety, confidence-gated precision across 788 word boundaries, and first-suggestion recovery after a 5-minute pause.

suites.label: Production Autocomplete Engine: Gemma 4 E2B vs. LFM2.5 1.2B
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · Release build · in-process llama.cpp
suites.dataset: 140 safety checks (28 scenarios × 5 passes) + 788 word positions in 96 synthetic phrases across 6 languages
suites.note: Accuracy counts held-back suggestions as misses; 'Right when shown' measures precision when the confidence gate displays text. In English, the two models are statistically tied (+1.1 pts, 95% CI −1.4 to +3.5).
suites.caveat: Engine timings exclude Accessibility field reads and overlay rendering. Synthetic phrases; some confirmed the hybrid decoder before shipping. On Cotabby's separate 782-checkpoint test, Gemma 4 E2B scored 32.7% vs Cotabby's 30.7%.

rows.note: LokalBot default. Stronger multilingual coverage (incl. Serbian) and higher precision when shown.
Lightweight preset. Statistically tied in English, 2–3× faster per keystroke, loads in 0.16 s.

suites.label: First Suggestion After a 5-Minute Pause (Metal Residency Fix)
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · macOS 27.2.1 · llama.cpp v1.0.0 (b12359)
suites.dataset: Gemma 4 E2B i1-Q6_K · single keystroke after 300 s idle vs immediate warm reference
suites.note: After llama.cpp's 180 s GGML_METAL_RESIDENCY_KEEP_ALIVE_S expires, ~3.4 GB of weights unwire (+50–80 ms) and the GPU clocks down (+10–15 ms). Decoding one throwaway token on wake/click/key with llama_synchronize and stripping it via seq_rm preserves the KV prompt.
suites.caveat: 30-minute pauses under heavy OS memory pressure (file paging) have not been re-measured yet. Four warm-up touches over 5 min added 18 mJ CPU energy (468 vs 450 mJ).

rows.model: Warm-up at first keystroke (45 ms debounce)
Periodic touch every 60 s while active
rows.note: Weights stayed wired, but GPU still clocked down (+10–15 ms).
Rejected: pins 3.4 GB wired even when away from Mac and doesn't wake GPU clocks.

categories.label: Local Hybrid Retrieval & Embedding Models
categories.summary: Head-to-head meeting retrieval across 232 public QMSum meetings (1,576 questions) comparing LokalBot's SQLite FTS5 + EmbeddingGemma 2 layer against GBrain v0.60, plus multilingual embedding comparisons.

suites.label: Hybrid Meeting Retrieval: LokalBot (SQLite) vs. GBrain (PGLite MCP)
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · shared EmbeddingGemma 2 Q8_0 server (496 MB peak)
suites.dataset: QMSum (232 public meetings, 129,177 turns, 2.1M words, 1,576 specific questions)
suites.note: Both hybrid configurations queried the exact same EmbeddingGemma 2 Q8_0 llama-server. Cloud Xeon keyword-only repeat matched accuracy exactly.
suites.caveat: GBrain beat LokalBot in keyword-only mode (2,000-char chunks vs single transcript rows) and ran without a hosted reranker or query expansion. Neither system automatically supersedes unlinked contradictory statements.

rows.note: +4.1 pts R@1 and +10.9 pts R@4 over GBrain Hybrid at 6.5× lower latency and ~20× lower process RAM.
Best keyword-only ranker (40.2% gold turn in evidence), but returns full ~97k-char transcripts.
Sends raw text without EmbeddingGemma query/document prompts; reranker disabled.
Ultra-fast lexical baseline; shows the +8.7 pt R@1 lift added by EmbeddingGemma 2.

suites.label: Multilingual Embedding Models (English + Serbian Latin/Cyrillic)
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · identical llama.cpp build
suites.dataset: 48 authored queries (24 English, 24 Serbian/Montenegrin Latin & Cyrillic) across 60 synthetic passages
suites.note: All models ran at Q8_0 on the same llama.cpp build with their native task prompts.
suites.caveat: On 48 correlated queries, the +6.3 pt top-1 gain over Harrier is within noise (95% CI −4 to +17 pts); EmbeddingGemma 2 won on matching quality at half the download, half the idle RAM, and 31% lower latency.

rows.note: LokalBot default. 23/24 EN, 20/24 SR; half the idle server RAM of Harrier (0.49 vs 0.97 GiB).
Previous default (22/24 EN, 18/24 SR).
Replaced in September 2026 pilot (35/48 top-1 on the same 48-query set).

categories.label: Meeting Extraction, Summaries & Native Tool Calling
categories.summary: Small local LLMs (2B–4B) evaluated on structured action-item extraction (ownership, deadlines, timestamps, Serbian Latin/Cyrillic, prompt injection) and native OpenAI-format tool calling in llama.cpp.

suites.label: Structured Extraction & Tool Calls on Apple Silicon
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · llama.cpp b10173 · -ngl 99 · 32K context
suites.dataset: 12 synthetic extraction cases (×2 repeats, 86 fields) + 6 single-turn native tool cases + 19K-token archive check
suites.note: In separate full-meeting replays on the same runtime, Qwen3.5 4B summarized a 26-min meeting (4,477 words) in 33.4 s warm / 59.8 s cold and a 91-min meeting (11,229 words) in 71.5–74.2 s (~85 tok/s decode).
suites.caveat: Bounded synthetic pilot, not a human-rated meeting summary quality corpus. MiniCPM5 2B also looped on a long summary in the Sept 7 pilot.

rows.note: LokalBot default. 6/6 native tool calls, 6/6 long-archive revisions, 4.18 GiB peak footprint.
Matched field accuracy only with 10.5× higher latency; still dropped Cyrillic fields.
42% smaller footprint, but made owner, timestamp, and Serbian Cyrillic errors.

suites.label: 4B Extraction & Tool Calls on Linux CPU: Spark-X2.6-4B vs. Qwen3.5 4B
suites.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X Ubuntu (CPU-only, 8 threads) · llama.cpp b11474 · 32K context
suites.dataset: Same 12 synthetic extraction cases (43 fields) + 6 tool cases + ~20K-token long-context pass
suites.note: Controlled Linux CPU screen evaluating Apache-2.0 Spark-X2.6-4B as a candidate replacement for Qwen3.5 4B.
suites.caveat: Linux CPU observations only, not Mac timings. Spark beat Qwen on short extraction (12/12 vs 10/12) but called search_meetings when asked to send email (no email tool exists) and ran 25% slower on ~20K context.

rows.note: Promising candidate; passed the unavailable-tool case when thinking was enabled (18.06 s).
Remains default pending full meeting-note + Apple Silicon testing.

categories.label: Screenshot OCR & Local Text-to-Speech
categories.summary: Opt-in on-device screen text extraction (Apple Vision vs. open-source OCR models) and local spoken summary synthesis (Kokoro 82M vs. Breeze TTS 2).

suites.label: Screenshot OCR — Synthetic Ground-Truth Set
suites.dataset: 5 generated desktop screenshots with exact ground-truth text manifests
suites.note: Measures multiset token precision/recall/F1 and reading-order character similarity.
suites.caveat: Small 5-image set; real desktop screenshots (next tab) widened the speed gap even further. PP-OCRv6 also needed ~15 s to load.

rows.note: Highest raw F1 (+0.003 over Apple Vision), but 57× slower with ~15 s model load.
LokalBot macOS default. 243.2 ms mean on 15 real desktop screenshots.
Hallucinated unrelated content on real desktop screenshots.

suites.label: Screenshot OCR — 15 Real Desktop Screenshots (Latency)
suites.dataset: 15 real LokalBot macOS screenshots (alternatives sampled on 3–5 images due to runtime)
suites.note: Every tested open-source OCR or VLM engine was 5× to 92× slower than Apple Vision on real full-screen captures.
suites.caveat: Token overlap is measured against Apple Vision rather than human transcription; see Ground Truth tab for absolute F1.

rows.note: Heavily truncated on full desktop screenshots.

suites.label: Local Spoken Summaries: Kokoro 82M vs. Breeze TTS 2
suites.hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · macOS 27.0 · audio.cpp v0.7.3 Metal vs installed Kokoro
suites.dataset: 255-word work summary narration + 356-word Qwen3-ASR content check
suites.note: Breeze TTS 2 sounded more natural to the owner and streams its first warm chunk in 0.88 s median, while Kokoro is 2.3× faster overall at ~8× lower memory.
suites.caveat: Breeze TTS 2 uses a non-commercial research license requiring a separate written agreement for product use; listening preference was unblinded from one listener.

rows.note: LokalBot default. 1/356 word discrepancy on ASR content check; tiny footprint.
More natural voice, but 7.9× peak memory and non-commercial license blocks shipping.

gaps.area: Apple Silicon variety (M1 / M2 / M3, 16 GB)
gaps.detail: Nearly all Mac numbers come from one M4 Max (48 GB). Timings and memory-pressure behavior on 16 GB M1–M3 Macs need community or secondary-machine runs.
Only the memory-restraint and Spark-X2.6 suites ran on Linux/Windows so far. Full sherpa-onnx ASR, pyannote/TitaNet diarization, and GPUI Vulkan/CUDA timings are still unmeasured.
Extraction tests cover structured fields, ownership, and tool calls, not blind human grading of full meeting recaps across diverse real calls.

gaps.area: Long idle pauses under RAM pressure
gaps.detail: The 5-minute autocomplete warm-up fix is verified (49–53 ms), but 30-minute pauses where macOS pages model files out under memory pressure remain unmeasured.
Diarization covers 4-speaker English AMI rooms; multilingual ASR probes are small FLEURS slices rather than full noisy meetings.
